messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.reasoning:
We need to calculate ΔS for heating from 0°C (ice) to 100°C water at constant pressure 1 atm.

But we have phase change: first melt ice at 0°C then heat liquid water up to 100°C. Also latent heat of fusion etc. We can compute using enthalpy changes divided by temperatures? Actually entropy change due to reversible process: dS_rev=δQ_rev/T. For each step:

Step 1: Melt ice at 0°C: δQ=m L_f where m=1 kg; Lf ~334 kJ/kg. At T=273 K. So ΔS1= Qrev /T = m*Lf / T_melt. But careful: melting occurs at constant temperature so reversible path would involve small increments near 273K. Use average T maybe 273K. We'll approximate as 273 K. So ΔS1 ≈ 1 * 334000 J / 273 K = about 1225 J/K.

Step2: Heat water from 0°C to 100°C: use Cp_water ~4184 J/(kg·K). Temperature increase ΔT=100 K. Entropy change integral ∫Cp/T dT = Cp ln(T_final/T_initial)= Cp ln(373/273). Compute Ln ratio: ln(373/273)=ln(1.3679)=0.3137. Multiply by Cp: 4184*0.3137≈1312 J/K.

Total ΔS_total = 1225 + 1312 = 2537 J/K approx.

Alternatively could also include vaporization but not needed because only to 100°C water remains liquid. Pressure 1 atm ensures boiling point 100°C. No further steps.

Thus answer around 2500 J/K.
